newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: KLI hits new low on forced selling.
newsitem.headline: KLI hits new low on forced selling.

text.p: Shares of Malaysian Kuala Lumpur Industries Holdings Bhd (KLI) sank to a new year low of Singapore $1.73 in active Tuesday morning trade on the back of forced selling, dealers said.
At 0245 GMT, shares of the property and and consumer products firm were around S$1.76. They led the actives with over four million shares traded.
Dealers said syndicates which pushed the stock up to a high of S$2.99 on March 13 were forced to sell after the Bank of Negara tightened loans on share trading on April 1, 1997.
"These syndicates are now forced to unwind their positions due to a lack of financing," said a Singapore broker.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
